## What's new in v2.6.1

### Redesigned History and dictation playback (#3147, #4586, #4611, #4703)

- **Three-tab diary:** History is rebuilt on a rebuildable local SQLite catalog with three tabs (Dictations, Transcripts, Meetings), grouped by day with 30-item paging, per-tab search, date filters, tab-specific filters, and `Select` to act on matching entries (`Delete all history` still clears every tab).
- **Dictation recordings (#4546):** With `Save dictation recordings` on, new eligible saved dictations keep a compressed audio recording on your Mac (AAC, 16 kHz mono, ~32 kbps, about 15 MB per hour) so you can play it back right from the dictation card with a voice waveform scrubber. Failed, cancelled, and Escape Recovery takes do not save audio, and recordings never leave your Mac.
- **Recordings settings:** A new `Settings > App Settings > Recordings` page lets you toggle `Save dictation recordings` (on by default), choose keep periods for dictations (`1 day`, `7 days`, `30 days`, or `Until I delete them` by default) and meetings (`30 days`, `90 days`, or `Until I delete them` by default), view storage usage, set a storage warning threshold (`1 GB`, `2 GB` default, `5 GB`, or `No warning`), pick `Ask me to free space` or `Remove oldest dictation recordings` (never deleting recordings marked `Keep this recording` or meeting audio), or run `Delete all dictation recordings` / `Delete all meeting audio` while keeping all text, notes, and summaries.
- **Upgrading History:** Installs that already completed setup before v2.6.1 see a one-time dismissible notice in History explaining dictation recordings.
- **Inline Dictations (#4555, #4616):** Dictation cards expand with `Show more` / `Show less`, show new dictations at the top, display changes on demand with `Show edits` (`Polished`, `Marked up`, `Original`), let you protect individual recordings with `Keep this recording`, switch back with `Restore original text` when polishing changed the text (ordinary dictations), delete audio without deleting text, and show the target app when saved.
- **Re-polish and preview (#4575):** Polish a saved dictation, file transcript or meeting transcript again and preview the new text before you keep it.
- **Transcripts (#4559, #4627, #4630):** Every imported file gets a card and full page (or its own window via `Open in new window`), inline title renaming, an adaptive docked player for the original file when available (`0.75×` to `2×` speed, `±15 s` skips, `Follow playback`), `Locate original…` when History can't open the original, and `Transcribe again with` using any installed speech engine when the original file is playable, without changing your dictation engine or altering the original file.
- **Meetings (#4561, #4571, #4575, #4629, #4723, #4725, #4727):** A unified meeting page lets you type structured notes (`Action item`, `Mark moment`, `Add quote`) beside the live transcript while recording, then play back with `Follow playback` and `Timestamps`, inspect speaking-time shares via the speakers button, and generate or compare AI summaries side by side (`Keep new` / `Keep current`). A meeting's first summary saves straight from the `Write summary with <model>` button; later summaries open `Compare summaries` so you can keep the one you like. History remembers your `Your notes` / `AI summary` tab choice for finished meetings with a transcript during the app session, and supported Apple Intelligence and Ollama `qwen3:8b` summaries can link back to matching `Your notes` and `Transcript` turns.

### Three EG-1 sizes on a new on-device engine (#4473, #4480, #4493, #4525)

- **About twice as fast:** On our tests, a typical EG-1 cleanup takes about 0.12 s on the new engine versus about 0.26 s for the previous EG-1, and scores higher on our sealed exam in English (97% vs 93%) and in ten other languages (86% vs 75%). EG-1 Mini and Micro are faster still.
- **Three on-device sizes (#4522):** Choose `EG-1` (4.7 GB download, 5.5 GB memory, 97% English / 86% in ten other languages, counting passes plus minor issues on our sealed exam), `EG-1 Mini` (2.1 GB download, 2.9 GB memory, 96% English / 82% international), or `EG-1 Micro` (805 MB download, 1.6 GB memory, 92% English / 71% international) in `Settings > AI Polish`. Each size includes its own learned-word checker download and can be removed independently.
- **Live memory bar (#4527):** Above and inside the EG-1 cards, a live memory bar shows your Mac's current memory in use (in binary GB matching Activity Monitor) alongside the size's projected memory, highlights `"Best for this Mac"`, and warns `"Won't fit right now. Close some apps or pick a smaller size."` when starting an idle size is projected to bring memory use above 90% (or `"Tight on this Mac"` when live usage is unavailable and the model alone needs more than half the Mac's memory).
- **New MLX engine and private helper communication (#4482, #4513, #4509):** All three EG-1 sizes run on the MLX-powered `envious-decode` helper (updated to `mlx-swift` 0.33.0 / MLX core v0.32.4 with the macOS 14 kernel fix). Both bundled local polish helpers (`envious-decode` and `llama-server` for S1-mini) now talk to EnviousWispr over Unix sockets inside private folders (`0700`) instead of local TCP ports and exit automatically when the app exits.
- **Upgrade behavior:** Eligible existing EG-1 installations stay on full `EG-1` by default and upgrade automatically from the older GGUF format to the new MLX download when model delivery is enabled and Setup is complete.

### Guided first-run Setup and larger starting window (#4528, #4590, #4639)

- **Redesigned Setup (#4563, #4592, #4594):** New installs walk through Welcome, Language, Speech model, AI polish, Permissions, Your key, a live Practice screen, and a closing film, with English and German interface support and Reduce Motion support. Language and Mac-memory rules recommend your speech engine and EG-1 size from `setup-rules.json`, and speech and local polish downloads start as you confirm each choice rather than downloading before Setup. Unfinished setups can resume from `Setup Required: Continue Setup…` in the menu bar.
- **Larger first-launch main window (#4639):** Fresh installs now open the main window at `1100×760` (up from `820×600`), within the `1440×900` point resolution of a 13-inch MacBook Air. Existing users keep their saved window size.

### macOS Share action for Transcribe a File (#4706)

- **Transcribe with EnviousWispr:** After completing Setup, share a supported single audio or video file (M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, CAF, MP4, QuickTime MOV, or FLAC) from Mac apps to `Transcribe with EnviousWispr`. Enable the action once in the Share menu, review your engine and AI Polish choices, and click `Start transcription` when ready. Original files stay untouched.

### Remove Parakeet and download progress (#4578, #4713)

- **Remove Parakeet too (#4584):** `Settings > Dictation Settings > Engine` and `Settings > EnviousMeet > Models` now offer `Remove` for Parakeet as well as Whisper, with both engines sharing the same Remove and `Set up model` controls, asking for confirmation when removing an active engine. A removed engine stays removed across relaunches and background upgrades until you explicitly choose `Set up model` (`Remove leftover files` clears incomplete removals).
- **Automatic meeting fallback and safety:** EnviousMeet uses your other downloaded speech engine when the picked one is removed, or displays a `"No speech engine downloaded"` notice if neither engine is installed. Leaving either Settings tab with an undownloaded engine selected offers `Set up model` or `Leave anyway` (with a switch-back option when available, or an `OK` notice while a download is running).
- **Parakeet download progress (#4713):** Foreground downloads and background upgrades for Parakeet now display a live progress bar alongside status and Cancel on the shared engine card.

### Six new cloud AI models (#4624, #4734)

- **Added to the cloud model list:** `gpt-6.2-sol`, `gpt-6.2-astra` (OpenAI), `claude-fable-5-2` (Claude), and `gemini-4-neon`, `gemini-4-hydrogen`, `gemini-4-carbon` (Gemini). Each passed three real dictations through the shipped connectors before it was added. Your model menu still comes from your provider's response for your own API key.
- **Delivery:** The list ships inside the app, and v2.6.0 and later also pick up list updates from `enviouswispr.com`.

### Cloud AI key checks at launch, Ollama catalog, and pill updates (#4721, #4675)

- **Launch cloud key checks (#4728):** At app launch (after setup), EnviousWispr runs a background model-list check and chosen-model probe for saved cloud API keys used by AI Polish, and includes meeting summary keys once EnviousMeet setup is complete (if the model-list check is inconclusive, it retries once on a later activation). Settings chips show `Key valid` or `Check failed` when available without needing to press Save again, and History banners and menu bar items route straight to `AI Polish` or `EnviousMeet > Summaries`.
- **Redesigned Self-Learning card (#4691):** The Self-Learning pill now displays for 12 seconds (up from 4), freezes its countdown while your pointer rests on it (resuming with at least 2 seconds left when you move away), and adds a `×` button to close immediately while keeping the word. Once you press Undo, it keeps running even if another dictation replaces the card.
- **Ollama library feed (#4463, #4621):** Added `gemma4:12b`, `llama3.2:3b`, `gemma3:4b`, and `mistral:7b` to the dynamic Ollama download list fetched from `enviouswispr.com`.

### Shortcuts, pasting, audio, EnviousMeet, and Settings fixes

- **5-second pause slider (#4678):** The `Pause duration` slider under `Dictation Settings > Engine > Stop recording on silence` now ranges from `0.5s` to `5.0s` in `0.25s` steps (default stays `1.5s`).
- **Push-to-talk with Caps Lock (#4647):** Push-to-talk with a single modifier key (such as Right Option or Fn/Globe) now triggers recording even when Caps Lock is switched on.
- **Telegram and TickTick pasting (#4669):** Verifies the target text field after Accessibility write errors to reduce duplicate pastes in Telegram and TickTick and keep self-learning edits tracking properly.
- **Fewer false "Copied" notices (#4459):** Improves field reading in WhatsApp and Messages and waits using per-app learned reveal patience before deciding a paste missed.
- **Dictation formatting (#4633, #4636):** Spoken number lists (such as `"40, 20, 10 percent"`) stay as lists instead of being summed into one number, and full-width CJK question marks (`？`) are recognized alongside `?` during polish checks.
- **Audio driver freeze protection and media resume (#4608, #4628, #4447):** Moves idle Core Audio device reads and audio-unit open/release calls onto bounded background lanes so the app stays responsive when certain third-party audio device operations stall (offering a `How to fix` link if the microphone fails to respond), and fixes paused media resume after dictation (including Spotify).
- **EnviousMeet improvements (#4431, #4439, #4442, #4478, #4600, #4595, #4614, #4705):** Adds support for company and US government Teams hosts (`teams.cloud.microsoft`, `gov.teams.microsoft.us`, `dod.teams.microsoft.us`), strips trailing `(Unverified)` / `(External)` tags and handles Teams compact screen-share windows so guests get named, improves Brave and Chrome Teams guest auto-recording, reduces false speaker splits in finished calls, names dominant one-on-one voices even with stray voice groups, prefers your Mac's language when turning Auto off for meeting transcripts if there is no supported saved choice, and prevents stale speaker/summary cancellation glitches.
- **Settings UI polish (#4541, #4615, #4617, #4715):** Updates Settings buttons and native square menu pickers (`Settings > App Settings > Recordings`, `Dictation Settings`, `EnviousMeet`, `Appearance`) for consistent rounded corners, row alignment, and native macOS menus.
